corrected_content.problem:
A body of mass $8kg$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F$, measured in Newtons $(N)$.
At time $t > 0$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t) = 2\sqrt{t}$ meters.
Calculate the magnitude of the force at time $t = 4$ seconds.
corrected_content.worked_solution: Differentiate position twice: $s'(t)=t^{-1/2}$ and $s''(t)=-\tfrac12t^{-3/2}$. Thus $F(t)=8s''(t)=-4t^{-3/2}\,\mathrm N$. At $t=4$, the force is $-1/2\,\mathrm N$, whose magnitude is $1/2\,\mathrm N$.
